newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Kim Hin exec charged with insider trades.
newsitem.headline: Kim Hin exec charged with insider trades.

text.p: Kim Hin Industries Bhd managing director Chua Seng Huat has been charged with two counts of insider trading involving the sale of 1.2 million shares, the Bernama news agency reported late on Wednesday.
It was the first insider trading case against an individual to be brought to court by Malaysia's regulatory body, the Securities Commission (SC), Bernama reported.
Chua, 35, pleaded not guilty to the charges and was released on 50,000 ringgit ($20,000) cash bail. Neither Chua nor any other Kim Hin official could be reached for comment on Thursday.

Chua was accused of misusing information to materially affect share prices in the sales to make a gain for himself. He was alleged to have committed the offences at the offices of a local securities firm on May 23 and June 26 1996, Bernama said.
The charges were brought under Section 90 of the Securities Industry Act 1983 and carry a fine of not less than one million ringgit and imprisonment of up to 10 years or both.
Kim Hin makes and sells building materials and is listed on the Main Board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange. Its stock was down 22 cents to 4.24 ringgit in late Thursday trading.
